bar.name: Onshape Sketch toolbar
bar.note: A separate bar from the feature toolbar. It appears only while a sketch is open.

ships.where: sketch-solve.ts constraint 'length' -- distance only, no angle

SketchFeature.shape 'circle' -- two points read as a diameter (lib/sketch-arc.ts circleOf()) -- plus the toolbar's Circle button (ModelEditor.tsx startCircleSketch()). Not a centre-plus-drag click: that needs the click-to-draw surface chrome2d names below, which still does not exist
lib/sketch-arc.ts filletCorner() -- trims both adjacent edges and inserts an arc via a bulge (tan(includedAngle/4)) -- wired to a per-corner radius field in the Rules panel (SketchConstraints.tsx).
ships.partial: corner-bearing sketches only, and reachable only from the Rules panel -- there is no click-a-corner-on-the-canvas surface, because there is no 2D canvas. A circle sketch renders no Rules panel and has no corners, so Round is unreachable for it by design. The refusal message that explains this has been wrong three times in a row, each generation naming a remedy the student could not reach; it now names none and just states what is true. This entry is an artefact under test like any other -- it overclaimed twice before saying this much.

build.name: the representation
build.why: DECIDED (build 1, panel-reviewed): SketchFeature gained two optional fields, additive to the existing points: Array<[number,number]> -- shape?: 'circle' (a tag, not an inference, read by circleOf()) and bulges?: Record<edge, number> (tan(includedAngle/4) on the edge leaving a corner, read by arcFromBulge()/tessellate() in lib/sketch-arc.ts). A sketch saved before this field existed has neither key and still loads, builds and renders exactly as before -- see scripts/check-sketch-compat.mjs. lib/sketch-solve.ts (the constraint relaxation solver) is UNCHANGED; both write-back paths already spread {...f, points}, so shape/bulges survive a solve untouched. Circle and Round a corner (fillet) ship on this. Arc, Rectangle and Polygon are unblocked by it but wait on chrome2d below, which is a different blocker

build.name: Rectangle
build.why: CORRECTED: never representation-blocked. newSketch() already emits a rectangle (four points, typed in by hand), and a straight-edged polyline was always exactly the right shape for one -- the representation panel added nothing this needed. Blocked on chrome2d: there is no click-to-draw surface, only a 3D-projected drag overlay (HandleOverlay.tsx) over the preview iframe, and two clicks on empty sketch-plane space is not something that overlay can place yet
build.landed: 2026-08-28 gauntlet round 3 (chrome2d piece 2), Corner Rectangle only -- click two diagonal corners on an empty sketch plane to place a real rectangle sketch. Built on chrome2d piece 1's planeAnchor() (a screen-projectable anchor at the plane origin, even with zero corners), reusing HandleOverlay's existing drag inverse-projection math for a click instead of a drag. Verified live via Playwright: real corner handles, correct RULES panel (opposite edges equal length), degenerate click (same point twice) correctly retries instead of creating a sliver, Escape cancels a half-placed rectangle. A real cross-piece bug (planeAnchor() set axisV but not paramV, so the runner never computed vx/vy and every click silently no-opped) was caught by this live check, not by code review or unit tests -- fixed and reverified.
build.note: Center Point Rectangle (centre + corner) still not built -- a second gesture for the same resulting shape, kept in `covers` here rather than moved to outOfScope so the checker keeps tracking it as real remaining work. By the reasoning already applied in outOfScope's 'Variants of tools we build' group, it's a candidate to reclassify as out of scope instead of building, but that's a policy call for review, not decided here.

build.name: Arc
build.why: CORRECTED TWICE. Not blocked on the representation (bulges expresses an arc exactly) and not blocked on a click-to-draw surface either: the two endpoints of the arc are the corners that are already there, so there is nothing to place and nothing to close. It was one missing write at the end of a finished pipeline -- the same shape as Equal, which shipped in `ships` for months with no control anywhere.
build.landed: 2026-09-01 gauntlet round 7, the 3 Point Arc half only, and reframed: an arc here is a BOW on an existing design edge, not a standalone curve. The 2026-08-28 design pass called this blocked on a general multi-point sketch tool; that was wrong. SketchFeature.bulges already expressed a curved edge end to end -- arcFromBulge, tessellate, outlineOf, HandleOverlay.projectOutline and the emitted polyArc all shipped -- and nothing wrote it (see 0580817: rounding writes `rounds`, so every `curved` branch in the panel was unreachable). What landed is the missing writer: bowOf/maxBow/bulgeFromBow/whyCannotBowEdge/bowEdge in lib/sketch-arc.ts, plus a 'Bow an edge:' row in SketchConstraints.tsx mirroring the Round and Chamfer rows, wired through bowSketchEdge() in ModelEditor.tsx. The stored number is the BOW (the sagitta, a distance) because every other number in that panel is a distance; the bulge is what is written, because unlike a round it is the parameter rather than a derived and clamped result, so it survives a corner drag the way a curve should. Capped at half the chord (a half circle). Verified live: a bowed edge draws as a real curve, reads 'curved', disables Across/Up/Length, refuses an over-ceiling bow with the ceiling named, and straightens back to 4 points at 0; measured in the gate through to the SOLID (a bowed extrude has more volume than the straight one), not just to the generated source.
build.note: NOT covered: Tangent Arc, which needs curved-to-curved tangency in lib/sketch-solve.ts -- the same wall Concentric and Tangent are already in outOfScope for. Also no canvas drag handle yet: the bow is linear in a perpendicular drag (scale 1, origin at the edge midpoint) so the existing one-axis HandleSpec fits it exactly, but the bulge would first have to become an emitted parameter rather than a literal, which is its own piece.

build.name: Polygon
build.why: CORRECTED: never representation-blocked -- N points is exactly what a closed polyline already is, and generating them is a for-loop the student can see. Blocked on chrome2d, same as Rectangle: there is nowhere to click to place the shape before the loop can size it
build.landed: 2026-08-28 gauntlet round 3 (chrome2d piece 3), Inscribed Polygon only, fixed at 6 sides -- click a center then a vertex; the clicked point becomes an actual corner (radius = click distance, angle = atan2 of the click), the rest of the hexagon generated from that. Reused piece 2's click-catcher and inverse-projection unchanged -- HandleOverlay.tsx needed zero edits. Verified live via Playwright: degenerate click (same point) stays in draw mode, a real placement produces a genuine regular hexagon (6 corner handles, 6 equal-length edges confirmed in the RULES panel).
build.note: Circumscribed Polygon (edges tangent to the circle, rather than vertices on it) is a second gesture for a related shape, not built here -- same reasoning as Rectangle's Center Point variant. No side-count picker either; fixed at 6. Both are candidates for outOfScope's 'Variants of tools we build' reasoning, left as a policy question for review rather than decided here.

build.name: Slice a corner
build.why: split out of the old 'fillet' item: Sketch Fillet shipped (Round a corner, via filletCorner() in lib/sketch-arc.ts -- rounds with an arc). A sketch-level CHAMFER slices the corner off flat instead: a straight replacement edge between two trim points, no bulge, no arc math. Same shape of work as the solid Angled Corner tool already does for a box or cylinder, not yet built for a sketch outline
build.landed: 2026-08-29, geometry (chamferCorner/maxChamferDistance/whyCannotChamferCorner in lib/sketch-arc.ts, chamfers?: Record<number,number> on SketchFeature, outlineOf() merges rounds+chamfers with round-wins on conflict) plus Rules-panel UI (a 'Chamfer a corner:' row mirroring 'Round a corner:' in SketchConstraints.tsx, wired via chamferSketchCorner() in ModelEditor.tsx). Verified live via Playwright: an ordinary chamfer sets and persists, an oversized request clamps to a measured ceiling instead of crashing, un-chamfering at 0 clears it, and the neighbour-interaction message correctly names the corner whose round ate the shared edge first ('That corner can only take a chamfer of 20.8 once corner 4 has taken its share of the edge between them').
build.note: outlineOf() processes rounds/chamfers descending by design corner index, so a corner's ceiling only reflects a HIGHER-indexed neighbour's trim, never a lower-indexed one (that neighbour is processed AFTER it, too late to matter within the same pass) -- this is pre-existing, documented behaviour inherited unchanged from Round, not something chamfer2d introduced, but it cost real debugging time to rediscover live and is worth knowing before testing this area again. Separately, a request landing almost exactly on a corner's own un-reduced design ceiling can report the 'own limit' wording even when a neighbour is the tighter real constraint (the reported number is still correct, just the suggested remedy can be the less-relevant one) -- an existing quirk shared with Round, not a chamfer2d regression, left as-is.

build.name: Guide line
build.why: a line that positions other lines without becoming part of the outline -- the sketch equivalent of a variable

build.name: Trim
build.why: the tool that makes drawing forgiving; without it a wrong line must be undone rather than fixed

build.name: Mirror
build.why: symmetry and repetition inside the sketch, where they cost one line of code instead of a boolean

build.name: more rules
build.why: two of Onshape's sixteen. Started as five; Coincident, Midpoint and Symmetric turned out to have nothing to attach to in this app's model and moved to outOfScope during the design pass
build.landed: 2026-08-29, solver (parallel/perpendicular Constraint kinds, a pinned-aware rotateEdgeBy primitive and a residual-units fix in lib/sketch-solve.ts, 34 assertions in scripts/sketch-solve-assertions.cjs) plus Rules-panel UI (a lower-triangular pair grid in SketchConstraints.tsx cycling none -> equal -> parallel -> perpendicular per unordered edge pair, pairs stored canonically as edge=lo/other=hi). The UI half also closed a pre-existing hole: Equal was listed in ships with no control anywhere in the panel, so it could not be created, seen or removed. scripts/check-constraint-ui.mjs now reads the Constraint union out of the solver and fails if any kind has no control, comments stripped first so prose cannot satisfy it.
build.note: an intentionally-impossible 3-way perpendicular on a triangle does not converge -- it burns all 300 solver iterations -- but never crashes or produces NaN, and correctly reports overConstrained so the existing 'these rules disagree' line fires. Accepted as a documented, bounded limitation: a student has to deliberately construct it, and 300 iterations at this sketch size is not a performance concern.

build.name: the bar itself
build.why: CORRECTED: the bar already exists -- ModelEditor.tsx's .model-tools has grouped buttons, a FlyoutButton that collapses variants under a caret (the same drop-down pattern Onshape's own tools.htm describes), and a search box with matches() filtering, same as the feature toolbar. The Sketch group is the first group on it and now has three buttons (Sketch, Circle, Corner). What is genuinely missing: a click-to-draw SURFACE. The sketch editing surface is a 3D-projected drag overlay (HandleOverlay.tsx) over the preview iframe -- corners are dragged, not placed by clicking empty sketch-plane space -- so Rectangle, Arc and Polygon above are blocked here, on interaction, not on the representation panel this item used to gate them on

outOfScope.why: a spline's control points are a genuinely different mental model, and nothing in a first-year CS course needs a conic. The solver would also have to grow curvature continuity, which is a term no fourteen-year-old should meet in week three
each projects existing 3D geometry into the sketch plane, which needs addressable faces and edges. Same B-rep wall the feature toolbar hit
file import into a sandboxed iframe, plus a font pipeline for Text. The bundle does carry vectorText, so Text is the one here worth revisiting if a lesson wants a name plate
each is reachable once the representation lands, and none is needed before it. Queued behind the panel's decision rather than refused on principle -- revisit after the shape work

outOfScope.group: Variants of tools we build (4 tools)
outOfScope.why: a second way to draw a thing the student can already draw. Onshape offers them because a professional wants the fewest clicks for their particular case; a beginner offered two ways to draw a circle learns that there are two ways to draw a circle

outOfScope.group: Constraints the solver cannot express (3 tools)
outOfScope.why: concentric and tangent need arcs to exist first and then need the solver to handle curved-to-curved conditions, which lib/sketch-solve.ts does not do. Automatic inferencing is a whole guessing engine on top of that. Reconsider once arcs land

outOfScope.group: Constraints with nothing to attach to (3 tools)
outOfScope.why: not a solver limitation -- a model-shape one. A sketch here is always ONE closed polygon, so there are no free points to make coincident, no second entity to be symmetric about, and every corner is already exactly the join of its two edges, which is the whole of what Coincident would assert. Midpoint needs a point that is not a corner, and this model has no such thing. All three were in the constraints item until the design pass found they had no referent; revisit if free points or a second sketch entity ever land

a point that is not a corner of the outline has nothing to reference it. In Onshape a sketch point is what a Hole feature snaps to; our Hole positions itself from its target's own centre instead, so a free point would be a dot the student can place and nothing can use. Revisit if Hole ever learns to snap.
